newsitem.title: POLAND: Eurobond cheaper vs domestic financing -Poland min.
newsitem.headline: Eurobond cheaper vs domestic financing -Poland min.

text.p: Polish Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko said on Tuesday foreign budget deficit financing, such as the country's mark-denominated Eurobond issue earlier this year, was cheaper than domestic financing.
Kolodko's statement came as a response to the central bank's call to finance the budget deficit domestically.

"Poland is considering all types of financing...(but) the Eurobond issue was cheaper than other, domestic types of financing this year," Kolodko told a parliamentary committee meeting debating next year's budget draft.

On Tuesday, the National Bank of Poland (NBP) reiterated its offer to lower its obligatory reserves if next year's budget deficit was not financed by foreign sources, which the central bank said would be more costly for the economy.

"One has to very carefully consider a foreign loan which would finance the budget deficit next year because, perhaps it will turn out that financing in Poland will be cheaper and with this goal (in mind), we are willing to lower obligatory reserves," said Witold Kozinski, deputy NBP head, also present.
Kozinski said, however, that a cut in obligatory reserves would likely create a temporary increase of money supply and create addiditonal inflationary pressure.
"We were never close to the idea of restricitve monetarism, quite the opposite, we believe money (supply) has its meaning...it is not the sole factor of price growth," he said.

The central bank had said that foreign financing created additional growth of domestic currency and was less profitable for the country because interest payments or taxes would be shipped abroad instead of remaining in Poland.
